title: Depth formula for a flat local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m_R)$ and $(S,\mathfrak m_S)$ be Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] local rings (commutative rings with exactly one maximal ideal) and $\varphi:R\to S$ a ring homomorphism which is local, i.e. $\varphi(\mathfrak m_R)\subseteq\mathfrak m_S$, and flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Let $\mathfrak m_RS$ be the ideal of $S$ generated by $\varphi(\mathfrak m_R)$; then $S/\mathfrak m_RS$ is a Noetherian local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_S/\mathfrak m_RS$ (the closed fibre). Then $\operatorname{depth}(S)=\operatorname{depth}(R)+\operatorname{depth}(S/\mathfrak m_RS)$, where the depth of a local ring is its depth as a module over itself [def-weil-pbc-depth], with values in $\{0,1,2,\dots\}\cup\{\infty\}$ and $a+\infty=\infty$.

proof.text: Let I=m_R S. Locality gives I⊆m_S and I≠S. Use Mathlib quotient nontriviality, the surjective local-ring construction, quotient Noetherianity and maximal-ideal mapping to obtain every closed-fibre structure clause. Bound the depths of R and S/I by their support dimensions, which are their ring dimensions. Finite local Krull dimension shows these depths are finite. Choose natural numbers a,b for them.

proof.text: Prove uniformly by induction on n that every flat local map A→B with source-plus-fibre depth n has target depth n. At n=0 both depths vanish. The maximal ideal is an associated prime of each ring: otherwise the nonzerodivisor lemma gives a singleton regular sequence in it, forcing depth at least one directly from the supremum definition. Use the Noetherian associated-prime characterization to choose z in A and ybar in the fibre with annihilator their maximal ideals. Lift ybar to y in B.

Flat annihilator base change gives Ann_B(φ(z))=m_A B. For b in B, bφ(z)y=0 iff by is in m_A B iff its fibre class kills ybar iff the class of b is in the fibre maximal ideal iff b∈m_B. Hence φ(z)y is nonzero and annihilated exactly by m_B. Every nonempty regular sequence in m_B would start with an injective multiplication killing this nonzero element, a contradiction. The defining supremum is therefore zero.

At successor n+1 apply the compatible quotient reduction. It produces a flat local map A/J→B/K between Noetherian local rings for which the sum of source and fibre depths plus one is the old sum. Cancel the finite summand 1 in ℕ∞ to get sum n. Apply the induction hypothesis to this quotient map and use the other reduction equality depth(B)=depth(B/K)+1 to get depth(B)=n+1.

lean.statement: theorem depth_eq_add_of_flat_local {R : Type u} {S : Type v} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsNoetherianRing S] [IsLocalRing R] [IsLocalRing S] (φ : R →+* S) [IsLocalHom φ] (hflat : φ.Flat) : let I : Ideal S := (maximalIdeal R).map φ IsNoetherianRing (S ⧸ I) ∧ ∃ hlocal : IsLocalRing (S ⧸ I), letI := hlocal (maximalIdeal S).map (Ideal.Quotient.mk I) = maximalIdeal (S ⧸ I) ∧ depth (R := S) S = depth (R := R) R + depth (R := S ⧸ I) (S ⧸ I)
